editorial.headline: Industrial Estate Management: Open Nationally and Available in Bali
editorial.standfirst: At Besar scale, this activity manages integrated industrial-estate land and infrastructure, with 100% foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Industrial-estate management under KBLI 68122 concerns a single, continuous expanse of land made into an industrial estate: a place where industrial activity is concentrated and supported by facilities and infrastructure. The work is the management of that estate land and of its supporting elements, which are developed and managed by the estate manager. In practical terms, the activity is defined by stewardship of an integrated industrial setting, not by a disconnected site-by-site arrangement.

The record opens the activity only at the Besar scale. That makes the estate manager—the party developing and managing the supporting facilities and infrastructure—the central registrant in view. The scale is substantive, not incidental: it is the only scale listed as open. A founder considering the activity should therefore frame it around management of a fully formed industrial area, with land in one expanse and the support infrastructure that enables the concentration of industrial activity.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. There is consequently no foreign-equity cap below full ownership in the national figure supplied for this activity. The national reference recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That openness belongs to industrial-estate management as described here and to the Besar scale stated in the record; it does not need embellishment with unprovided requirements or thresholds.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. Its standing is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—so the activity is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. The provincial moratorium is described as island-wide and permanent, with Low and Medium-Low OSS risk as its stated trigger. At Besar scale, this activity sits outside that block. The honest result is clear: a foreign investor may register this activity in Bali at Besar scale, with the same 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling, because it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: At Besar scale, industrial-estate management is open nationally to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA in Bali.
